name: Chat Composer
hint: Type a few lines, drop a file on it, press / or @, switch to Quick, then send and watch your text land in the thread.
description: The message composer of an AI chat product (shown as Margin, a research assistant that reads the files you give it), under a short thread. It changes shape with the conversation: the field grows on a spring to fit what you write (up to a row limit or 40% of the panel, then scrolls), Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a line and IME composition never sends. Files arrive by button, paste or drag-and-drop and fly into a tray as chips with a type glyph, upload progress and remove; errors are typed and stay on the chip (Over 20 MB, can't read .key files, a model that can't read files with a one-tap fix). A model menu lists each model with what it is good at and a capability mark, and changing it updates the hints: the attach button explains why it is off for a text-only model. The send button morphs in place through the AI SDK states: disabled while empty, Send, submitted, Stop while the reply streams, Retry with the reason above the field on error. On send the text lifts out of the field and settles into the thread as your bubble with a measured FLIP while the field springs back to one line. Slash commands and @-mentions of attached files open a listbox above the caret line. A quiet footer shows context used as a thin meter and the shortcuts. Phones get a bottom-docked composer that follows the keyboard through visualViewport, bottom sheets for the model and attach menus, and a snap rail for the tray. Reduced motion drops the flight: the bubble appears and the field resets.
intents: chat input for an AI assistant with file attachments

usage: A message composer with a thread above it. Handle `onSend({ text, attachments, model })` and drive the state from your stream (e.g. the AI SDK's useChat): `status` (ready, submitted, streaming, error) is the busy state you own, `messages` ({ id, role: user|assistant, text, files?, cites?, state?, model? }) is the thread, `onStop()` and `onRetry()` are the stop and retry buttons. The text is `value` / `defaultValue` / `onChange`. Attachments: uncontrolled, picked, pasted or dropped files are checked against `accept` and `maxSizeMB` (or your `validate`), rejected ones show your message on the chip and call `onReject(file, error)`, accepted ones call `onAttach(files)` and sit in the tray as { id, name, size, status: done, file } until sent; nothing is uploaded by the component. To own uploads pass `attachments` ([{ id, name, size, status: uploading|done|error, progress 0-1, error?: { code, message, detail?, fix?: { label } } }]) with `onRemoveAttachment(id)` and `onFixAttachment(id, code)`. Models: `models` ([{ id, name, note, caps?: [files|fast|cites], context? }]) with `model` / `defaultModel` / `onModelChange`; a model whose caps leave out files disables attaching and explains why. `commands` feeds the / menu (`onCommand(command)`), attached files feed the @ menu, `library` adds ready files to the attach menu. Inside a <form>, `name` puts the text in FormData, Enter or Send submits the form and reset clears it. `disabled` with `disabledText`, `error` for a field error; `aria-label` and `aria-describedby` go to the field, other unknown props to the root. `demo` fills everything left out with the sample research thread and plays its scripted send and simulated replies.
